guide.biggerreactorsrework.index.howto: Click a topic or turn the page.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.recipe_missin: Recipe not available on this server.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.start: Start with materials, a passive reactor, fuel and an energy consumer. Fuel → reactor → FE. In an active circuit: fuel → reactor → vapor → turbine → FE. FE measures stored energy; FE/t measures generation. mB measures fluid; mB/t measures flow. RPM measures rotor speed.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.mater: Materials follow a progression: collect uranium, smelt fuel, produce cyanite in a reactor, recover blutonium and craft ludicrite. Recipes below use world data.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.react: Casing closes the structure; glass can occupy faces while casing remains on edges. The terminal shows the panel and errors. Internal fuel rod columns end at a control rod in the roof. Access ports receive fuel and remove waste. Power taps export FE in passive mode; coolant ports serve active mode. Manifolds transfer internal heat. Redstone automates commands and sensors; computer integration is optional. Computer ports provide optional telemetry and controls through CC:Tweaked or OpenComputers when a compatible version is installed.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.build: Model dimensions are external. Close the floor, walls and roof; install terminal, access port and power tap on faces. Keep each fuel column continuous up to its control rod. Feed fuel through access, connect a consumer and activate at the terminal. If assembly fails, read the terminal message before rebuilding. The larger model fills space around the column with graphite.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.react: The terminal separates fuel and casing temperatures, generation, consumption, fuel, waste and storage. Increasing rod insertion reduces the reaction; withdrawing rods increases it. Stored heat continues to dissipate after shutdown. Check automatic or manual waste ejection and output space. Chunk unload remembers the desired activity; breaking a part turns the machine off.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.moder: Solid moderators affect only direct FE generation. Free fluids cannot be placed inside either reactor mode. In liquid mode, solid moderator blocks behave exactly like air; coolant is transported inside manifolds. Compare absorption, efficiency, moderation and conductivity for solid layouts using the same fuel and rod settings.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.repro: Insert cyanite and supply the indicated fluid and energy. Leave space to extract blutonium from the output. Configure item, fluid and energy faces in the side tab; automation can supply the machine and remove its product. If work stops, check ingredients, water, FE and output space. Recovery is partial: it does not provide infinite fuel. Liquid Obsidian is manufactured cold; only the reactor supplies its heated form. Ordinary lava cannot supply this circuit.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.activ: Direct generation uses solid moderators and power taps. Liquid cooling requires coolant ports and manifolds directly beside fuel rods; more contact increases heat exchange. Water becomes steam. Make Liquid Obsidian from obsidian and water in the Industrial Processor. The reactor produces identified heated Liquid Obsidian, which the heat exchanger cools back while generating steam. Vanilla lava is not accepted. Optional liquid sodium and Cryo Fuel appear only when installed. Supply the cold coolant and remove the hot product; automatic burn reduction respects your control rod settings. Open the Statistics side tab to compare potential and current conversion in mB/t. The turbine may return condensed water or discard it with an external water supply.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.turbi: Casing and glass close the turbine; the terminal controls it. Exactly two bearings delimit a continuous shaft. Blades connect to the shaft. Coils are registered material blocks around the rotor, on layers separate from blades. Ports admit and remove fluids; taps export FE. The redstone port works without computers. Consult current efficiency, extraction and bonus properties rather than assuming a block from another mod is accepted. Computer ports provide optional telemetry and controls through CC:Tweaked or OpenComputers when a compatible version is installed.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.build: Align both bearings and fill the shaft between them. Blades must connect correctly and coils must surround the rotor. Configure inlet and outlet, connect energy and supply steady vapor. Check activity, nominal flow, RPM and coil engagement in the panel. Disengaging coils reduces extraction from the rotor. Vent modes affect liquid return. Historical RPM values are not a guaranteed target for this rework. Right-click a shaft, existing blade or bearing with a blade to add one real blade at a time, ring by ring and level by level. The base outline, both aligned bearings and continuous shaft are enough to add blades before closing the walls or roof. Sneak with an empty hand to remove the last blade. Sneak with blades for manual placement. Breaking a shaft segment collects only its attached blades when using the correct tool; inventory overflow drops beside the shaft.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.excha: The exchanger transfers heat between two independent circuits without mixing their fluids. Build a shell, condenser and evaporator channels, and four ports: two per circuit. Each channel connects to ports of its own type. Place condenser channel faces against evaporator channel faces: every shared face increases direct heat transfer capacity. Corner or edge contact does not count. With a block of space between channels, heat passes through the interior, transfer is slower and stabilization takes longer. More channels alone do not replace more contact. In Statistics, check contact faces, temperatures and potential/current conversion. Potential assumes steady operation, full inlets and free outlets; during startup some heat warms the structure itself. Check supply and outlets for both circuits. The example keeps the fluids separate while placing the two channel types against each other. Computer ports provide optional telemetry and controls through CC:Tweaked or OpenComputers when a compatible version is installed.
tooltip.biggerreactorsrework.channel_con: Place a face against the other circuit's channel.
More contact faces = greater direct heat transfer.
A gap makes heat transfer and stabilization slower.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.autom: Separate fuel input, cyanite output, reprocessing and blutonium return. Configure fluid and energy ports individually. Turbine redstone controls activity, coils or flow percentage: level responds to signal changes; pulse acts on the rising edge. RPM, battery (%), vapor and liquid (mB) sensors use ≥, ≤ or an inclusive range. The last valid command wins. Recipe viewers are optional; the guide and machines work without them.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.effic: Compare power, consumption per time and energy per fuel unit separately. Warm up and stabilize the machine; record version, configuration, fuel, insertion and supply. Measure generation and energy actually extracted. Change one variable at a time: moderator, rod layout, cooling, flow, rotor or coils. Models illustrate construction and connections; they do not promise fixed production or output measured under different settings.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.troub: Cannot assemble: read the terminal; check shell, dimensions, columns and internal parts. No production: check fuel, rods and mode. No energy output: check tap, connection and destination capacity. No waste output: check ejection, direction and space. Reprocessor stopped: check recipe, ingredients, fluid, FE and output. Turbine spins without generation: check coils, vapor and FE extraction. Exchanger stopped: check four ports, circuits and transitions. Stops later: check full destinations, continuous supply and loaded chunks. Before joining independent machines, empty their inventories; joining two independently stocked machines is blocked to preserve their contents.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.cover.title: BiggerReactors-Rework
guide.biggerreactorsrework.cover.intro: From your first reactor to vapor circuits. Recipes and tables follow world data.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.material.uran: Find uranium ore in stone or deepslate. Mining supplies raw uranium chunks; smelt them in a furnace for ingots. Collected ore blocks also have smelting recipes. Icons below cycle through accepted inputs. Use the ingots as reactor fuel.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.material.grap: Smelt coal or charcoal in a furnace to obtain graphite ingots. There is no need to craft and unpack a storage block. Graphite is used in components and can serve as a moderator.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.material.cyan: Insert uranium ingots through the access port of an assembled reactor and activate it at the terminal. Fuel consumption accumulates cyanite as waste. Remove it through the access port using manual or automatic ejection. The diagram illustrates operation, without implying an instant ingot-for-ingot conversion.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.material.blut: Blutonium is produced in the Industrial Processor, a single-block machine. First craft the machine using the recipe below. Then use it to process cyanite as shown in the processing card.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.material.ludi: Combine blutonium, ender pearls, emerald blocks and a nether star at a crafting table. This recipe produces a ludicrite block for turbine coils. An alternative appears only when registered in the world.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.viewer.glass_: Yellow: positions accepting casing or glass. Edges and corners require casing. Ports and functional parts are not replaceable.

Corners and edges form a casing frame. Ordinary positions inside each face accept either casing or the machine’s own glass. Hover the “Casing or glass” row to highlight these positions in yellow. The preview alternates both options; the quantity is shared, not added. Drag the model to rotate; use the mouse wheel over it to adjust zoom.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.limits.reacto: The reactor supports external dimensions from %s × %s × %s to %s × %s × %s blocks under current configuration (length × height × width). Both energy and vapor modes use the same reactor. Intermediate sizes must meet assembly rules. The models below are small examples; the maximum is described only in this text.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.limits.turbin: External turbine limits: minimum %s × %s × %s and maximum %s × %s × %s blocks under current configuration (length × height × width). The shaft, two bearings, blades and coils must also meet assembly rules. The 3D model is an example, not the maximum size.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.limits.exchan: External heat exchanger limits: minimum %s × %s × %s and maximum %s × %s × %s blocks under current configuration (length × height × width). Both circuits and their four ports are still required. The 3D model shows a small assembly, not the maximum.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.batte: Casing and glass close the battery. The terminal shows the charge and the last tick's input and output, and holds two item slots: one drains an item into the battery, the other charges an item from it. Energy ports connect the battery to cables: a wrench switches a port between input and output, and right-clicking opens its screen. Cells fill the inside. Each cell stores %s and adds %s to the input limit and the same again to the output limit, so the battery grows linearly with its cells. Each cell keeps its own share of the energy, so a charged cell that is broken keeps it as an item and brings it into the next battery it joins.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.build: Build a rectangular shell with casing on every edge and corner and fill the inside with cells; empty space inside is allowed. A working battery needs a terminal, at least two energy ports and at least one cell. If every port points the same way when the battery assembles, one of them is switched so there is an input and an output. Right-click any block of the assembled battery to open the terminal; ports open their own screen. Energy enters through input ports and leaves through output ports within the per-tick limits shown in the terminal. Taking the battery apart loses no energy: the cells keep it, and the next battery adds up what its cells bring.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.limits.batter: External battery limits: minimum %s × %s × %s and maximum %s × %s × %s blocks under current configuration (length × height × width). The terminal, two ports and at least one cell are still required. The 3D model is an example, not the maximum size.

guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.activ: Automatic protection keeps liquid-cooled operation stable. Hot coolant or steam retained at the outlet gradually reduces fuel burn and coolant conversion. A full output stops both until space is available. The system observes the lowest output stock over one second: normal pipe batches cleared within that interval do not reduce performance. Persistent occupancy sets a linear limit; 50% retained occupancy allows up to 50% operation. Once extraction resumes, this limit recovers gradually over about one second. A full cold inlet causes no penalty; provide enough cold coolant and remove the hot product to use the available capacity. Solid-mode generation is unaffected.
guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.excha: Steam retained at the outlet gradually limits both steam production and hot-to-cold coolant conversion. A full steam output blocks both conversions. Normal pipe batches cleared within one second do not cause this penalty, and operation recovers gradually after extraction resumes. Full water or hot-coolant inlets and stored cold coolant do not impose a gradual penalty. However, a completely full cold output has no room for more cold coolant; clear it to continue that conversion. Stored heat remains accounted for while processing is limited. Check Statistics to distinguish retained steam, missing inputs and a full cold output. Turbine flow and condensate-discard controls are unchanged.

guide.biggerreactorsrework.calculator.he: The calculator looks for a plant that reaches the generation you ask for, with the materials you choose. Type the target in RF/t (the same as FE/t in this mod), pick a solid reactor and its moderator, or a liquid-cooled reactor with its coolant and the turbine coil, and press Calculate. Water goes straight from the reactor to the turbine; other coolants pass through a heat exchanger that boils the turbine's water. Each candidate is simulated with the machines' own rules, with finite fluid charges and the ports touching each other, and the smallest plant that reaches the target is validated again, with the rod setting that burns the least fuel. The result shows the sizes, the functional parts, the charges and the settings, and View layout shows every block. Closing the guide discards the form and a calculation in progress. Recent keeps the last three results and Save keeps up to 50 until you remove them; both are kept between restarts, per player and per world or server.

guide.biggerreactorsrework.content.batte: The optional Redstone Sensor replaces a wall block, away from edges and corners. It emits strength 15 from the outer face when the chosen condition is met: at or above a percentage, at or below a percentage, full or empty. Each sensor saves its own settings. Full and empty mean exactly 100% and 0%. A disassembled battery emits no signal. To control a turbine, use at or below 90% and connect the output to a turbine redstone port configured as Activity / Level: below the limit the turbine runs, above it the signal stops. The sensor only reports charge; redstone wiring and the receiving machine determine the action.
